title: Geometric and levelwise open extension on ringed sequence sites
statement:
Let $j:V\hookrightarrow W$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion], and fix small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be a strict tower of commutative ring sheaves on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, set $C_n=j^{-1}B_n$, and use their ringed sequence sites and strict semilinear module categories $\mathscr S_W(B),\mathscr S_V(C)$ [lem-pur-sequence-site-completion-projection, def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. The levelwise inverse image induces a geometric morphism $\widetilde j$ of sequence topoi; it is localization at the constant sequence of the subterminal sheaf represented by $V\to W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Its ring-sheaf inverse image identifies $B_\bullet$ with $C_\bullet$.

Under the canonical equivalences with semilinear systems, module extension by zero along $\widetilde j$ [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] identifies naturally with the exact functor $J:\mathscr S_V(C)\to\mathscr S_W(B)$ whose value at level $n$ is $j_{!,B_n}M_n$. For every $m\ge n$ its actual restriction-form transition is $j_{!,B_m}(a_{m,n})$ followed by the canonical coefficient comparison $j_{!,B_m}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}j_{!,B_n}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. This comparison is identity on underlying additive sheaves, is compatible with composition of coefficient maps, and is compatible with the units and counits of open extension/restriction. The same identifications hold for termwise derived descent on the ordinary unbounded derived system categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], naturally on derived morphisms. If compatible homomorphisms from a commutative ring $R$ to $\Gamma(W,B_n)$ specify scalar actions, $J$ preserves their actual scalar endomorphisms [def-weil-linear-functor].
